common_name: Pastel Splendor Itoh Peony (Lavender-Cream Intersectional Hybrid Peony)

planting.note: Plant divisions in fall in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade, setting eyes shallow and leaving the clump undisturbed once established.

directions: Pastel Splendor is an Itoh intersectional peony bred by Anderson and Seidl in Wisconsin, bearing single to semi-double, 4-6 inch blooms of pale lavender-pink fading to cream near the center, with dark reddish-purple flares at the base of each petal and multiple golden carpels. It is a vigorous, compact grower with an unusually high bud count and one of the longest bloom seasons among peonies, and like other Itoh hybrids its sturdy stems rarely need staking. Grow in full sun to part shade in fertile, well-drained soil, and leave the clump undisturbed for years to let flowering build.

common_name: Anderson's Kaleidoscope Itoh Peony (Streaked Rose-Pink Intersectional Hybrid Peony)

planting.note: Plant divisions in fall in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun, setting eyes shallow and leaving the clump undisturbed once established.

directions: Introduced in 2006, Anderson's Kaleidoscope produces ruffled, 5 inch semi-double flowers in deep pink, red, and cream streaks, with no two blooms identical and the coloring continuing to shift as each flower matures. It carries one bloom per upright, self-supporting stem and, like other Itoh hybrids, combines tree-peony-type foliage with the hardy, herbaceous growth habit of a garden peony. Grow in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil and expect bloom to improve as the clump matures.

common_name: Old Rose Dandy Itoh Peony (Purplish-Rose Blend Intersectional Hybrid Peony)

planting.note: Plant divisions in fall in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun, setting eyes shallow and leaving the clump undisturbed once established.

directions: Registered in 1993 from a cross made by Chris Laning, Old Rose Dandy bears single-form, notched-petal flowers that open yellow-beige washed with purplish rose and a large flare at the base of each petal; the purplish tones fade as the bloom ages while the flare color persists. It flowers prolifically on a medium-low, rounded, strong-growing bush in midseason to late midseason. Grow in full sun in fertile, well-draining soil and expect reliable, heavy bloom once the clump is established.

common_name: Yellow Heaven Itoh Peony (Red-Blotched Yellow Intersectional Hybrid Peony)

planting.note: Plant divisions in fall in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun, setting eyes shallow and leaving the clump undisturbed once established.

directions: One of the original intersectional crosses made by Toichi Itoh and later introduced by Louis Smirnow, Yellow Heaven is a cross of the herbaceous 'Kakoden' with the tree peony 'Alice Harding,' producing fragrant, ball-form, yellow flowers with red blotches at the center and good substance. It carries tree-peony-type foliage on an otherwise herbaceous plant habit, growing with excellent vigor and blooming in midseason. Grow in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil and expect improved flowering as the clump matures.

common_name: Yellow Dream Itoh Peony (Golden Ball-Form Intersectional Hybrid Peony)

planting.note: Plant divisions in fall in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun, setting eyes shallow and leaving the clump undisturbed once established.

directions: Yellow Dream is one of Toichi Itoh's original intersectional crosses between a tree peony and a herbaceous peony, prized by collectors for its place in Itoh-peony history. It bears large, fragrant, semi-double, ball-form flowers in rich golden yellow with a light red blotch at the center of each petal and an orange cluster of stamens, held on sturdy, self-supporting stems above finely cut, gray-green, tree-peony-type foliage that colors red in spring and fall. Grow in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil and expect strong midseason bloom with excellent vigor once established.

common_name: Lemon Dream Itoh Peony (Streaked Lemon-Yellow Intersectional Hybrid Peony)

planting.note: Plant divisions in fall in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun, setting eyes shallow and leaving the clump undisturbed once established.

directions: Bred by Roger F. Anderson, Lemon Dream is a fragrant Itoh hybrid bearing sturdy, prolific, semi-double lemon-yellow flowers irregularly streaked with lavender-pink, with mature plants occasionally producing pure yellow, pure lilac, or stippled blooms alongside the typical streaked flowers. Dark green, tree-peony-type foliage emerges rich red before turning green, on an upright plant that blooms midseason without needing staking. Grow in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil and expect bloom to improve as the clump matures.

common_name: Chief Black Hawk Itoh Peony (Darkest Red Intersectional Hybrid Peony)

planting.note: Plant divisions in fall in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun, setting eyes shallow and leaving the clump undisturbed once established.

directions: Bred by Anderson and Kornder and registered in 2008, Chief Black Hawk is considered the darkest Itoh peony known, bearing fragrant, semi-double, 5 inch flowers with a double ring of velvety, dark wine-red petals shimmering around soft yellow, pollen-free stamens. It forms a symmetrical, mounding, self-supporting plant that blooms in midseason. Grow in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil and expect improving bloom as the clump matures.
